gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_type_check (applies column affinities to a register block and enforces CHECK constraints before MakeRecord/Insert)
gaps.notes: F2.40 (2026-08-10): promoted partial→parity for the write affinity/STRICT/CHECK slice delivered; subquery/compound affinity residuals live under compile-affinity-rules-diverge-in-subquery-and-compound-contexts. Closed 2026-08-03 via four coordinated fixes. (A) ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN on a STRICT table now rejects a type-mismatched DEFAULT with 'type mismatch on DEFAULT' (existing rows only), matching SQLite instead of the row-level 'cannot store X value in Y column'. (B) i64 cast boundaries made exclusive at all six sites: a float exactly at i64::MIN/MAX (or beyond) no longer wraps, it errors 'integer overflow' per SQLite's cast semantics. (C) Comparison-affinity threading through a QueryContext: rowid and rowid-alias column references carry Integer affinity in comparisons (including IN lists via ApplyInComparisonAffinity), while NEW/OLD trigger pseudo-table columns carry NO affinity except rowid aliases and the rowid register, exactly per turso-src/core/translate/trigger_exec.rs:1043-1070 (SQLite forum 819f2d6627). (D) TRIM/LTRIM/RTRIM and nth_value boundary parsing now treat only ASCII whitespace as trimmable, so Unicode-space-padded values stay intact (SQLite trim is ASCII-only). Expected-failures count dropped by 13 (12 mapped + nth-value-unicode-whitespace-n-errors) with zero additions; full lane 3765/3765 passing. Two cases previously linked here (subquery-column-affinity-inheritance, range-scan-text-vs-int-affinity) are affinity-propagation issues in subquery/compound contexts and now track under compile-affinity-rules-diverge-in-subquery-and-compound-contexts; the two gencol_self_table_affinity_indexed_* cases were already closed by parser-indexed-by-hint.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/unnest.rs::try_rewrite_exists / try_rewrite_in / rewrite_as_semi_or_anti_join / can_rewrite_as_semi_join (v0.8.0-pre.7)
gaps.notes: Closed 2026-08-23. A top-level conjunctive correlated EXISTS / NOT EXISTS / direct positive IN over a single ordinary base table becomes an internal semi or anti join, so the inner table is materialized once per statement instead of being re-planned per outer row. The join projects only the left row shape and emits each left row at most once, so duplicate inner matches never multiply outer rows. It reuses the correlated subquery's statement-cached transient hash probe, which canonicalizes both sides of an equality under exactly the comparison affinity and collating sequence SQLite applies (numeric pulls non-numeric to numeric, TEXT pulls affinity-less to text, and the collating sequence follows operand order) and declines to prune when either side cannot be proven. Excluded: NOT IN, any subquery under OR, an outer join anywhere in the enclosing FROM clause, uncorrelated subqueries (already memoized), a WHERE clause with more than one top-level conjunct where any conjunct can raise on its input (AND short-circuits, so a join would either hide or invent an error), a subquery with DISTINCT/GROUP BY/HAVING/ORDER BY/window/LIMIT/OFFSET/aggregate, a joined/derived/CTE/view/virtual/table-valued or compound inner source, a null or subquery-bearing or non-deterministic inner WHERE, a correlation predicate that is not a plain inner=outer equality, an anti-join term that never reads the inner table, an IN whose operands or whose own inner WHERE can raise (IN scans its subquery to completion, so an error in a row after the first match must still surface), and an EXISTS whose select list binds a parameter. Bytecode lowering declines these joins (no VdbeJoinKind counterpart), so the rewritten select runs on the evaluator. EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN describe the un-rewritten statement. Evidence: src/Ahtola.Tests/SubqueryRewriteTests.cs.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/index_method/fts.rs:1856-1905 (Tantivy chunk-blob backing table + backing_btree index)
gaps.notes: Opened and closed 2026-08-24 by managed-index-methods-fts as a recorded divergence. A method index is a real sqlite_schema 'index' row with a real rootpage and an ordinary SQLite index b-tree; no page, cell or WAL format changed. A versioned state header rides in a trailing SQL comment on the index's sql text (the same mechanism already shipped for managed virtual tables), and the inverted index (terms, term frequencies, positions, column masks, tombstones) is DERIVED state rebuilt from the base rows inside the catalog snapshot, so rollback/savepoint/crash/VACUUM correctness is inherited. Ahtola does NOT synthesize FTS5 shadow tables and the file is NOT interoperable: stock sqlite3 cannot parse CREATE INDEX ... USING fts and reports a malformed schema for that row, exactly as it would for Turso. Do not describe this layout as SQLite-compatible. Review follow-up 2026-08-24: postings are generation stamped (an upserted or reused rowid retires its previous terms immediately); ranking-only plans retain every unranked base row and are priced accordingly; attachments are published only on success and dropped on every failure; REINDEX/Optimize build detached and publish atomically; DROP INDEX runs Destroy; state envelopes are decoded only for USING-method declarations, length-bounded before the base64 decode allocates, and fully field-validated; detail/columnsize/gram options are implemented or rejected; folding preserves exact source offsets across combining marks and surrogate pairs; prefix limits count live terms only; maintenance is revision-aware through RowStore.Revision plus a per-table mutation journal fed by ReportRowChange, with PreCommit run inside the commit; and the foundation is method generic (generic result rows, per-method planner adapters with KNN hooks, arbitrary SqlValue arguments, no FTS casts in the core), proven by a non-FTS KNN method that plans and executes end to end.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/index_method/toy_vector_sparse_ivf.rs (sparse component inverted index, jaccard only, delta/scan_portion/scan_order heuristics); turso-src/core/index_method/mod.rs
gaps.notes: Opened and closed 2026-08-24 by managed-vector-index as a recorded divergence. Ahtola ships CREATE INDEX ... USING vector on the managed index-method foundation, but it is NOT a port of Turso's toy_vector_sparse_ivf: that file is a jaccard-only sparse component inverted index over vector32_sparse columns, backed by two real b-trees Ahtola has no per-statement write API for, and pruned by three unbounded heuristics (delta, scan_portion, scan_order) with no recall bound, no k-means, no centroids, no training, no rebuild/optimize, no versioned state and no cost model. Ahtola's method is an Ahtola-designed IVF-Flat with an exactness certificate: k-means centroids are durable in the versioned catalog state envelope, assignments/postings/radii are derived from the base rows, and a list is skipped only when a proven inequality (triangle inequality for l2, angular for cosine, Cauchy-Schwarz for dot, exact integer Hamming for float1bit), widened by a floating-point slack sized to the reported distance's accumulation width, shows no member of it can enter the top-k; otherwise more lists are probed, degrading to a full scan rather than to a wrong answer. What is carried over from Turso is the method/attachment/cursor shape from index_method/mod.rs, results_materialized=true, TransactionalBackingStore, and the 'ORDER BY distance LIMIT ?' query shape in both argument orders. Honest limits: sparse vectors and metric='jaccard' are rejected at CREATE INDEX rather than silently downgraded; exact=0 (approximate mode) is rejected, so no configuration returns a different row set than the unindexed query; a single NULL or otherwise invalid indexed value declines the plan entirely, because the scalar form of the query raises on that row and an index that skipped it would turn an error into a result set; and data with no exploitable cluster structure re-prices the index out of the plan (the cost model measures reranked rows, not probes) instead of becoming approximate. Supported: float32/float64/float8/float1bit encodings under l2/cosine/dot, minus l2-over-float1bit which the scalar evaluator does not define. See docs/managed-vector-index.md.
